name: raw-icmp-socket
why: socket(AF_INET, SOCK_RAW, IPPROTO_ICMP) by a non-allowlisted binary is the Strategy 2 chokepoint
source: synthetic: shape of normalize() output for the atomic's own socket() record

name: raw-ipv6-nonblocking
why: AF_INET6 with SOCK_RAW|SOCK_NONBLOCK is the same chokepoint; the flag bits must not hide it

name: stream-socket
why: same family and syscall, SOCK_STREAM instead of SOCK_RAW: the a1 constraint must be load-bearing (the afinet_stream_socket.c mutant, offline)

name: packet-socket-raw
why: SOCK_RAW on AF_PACKET (0x11) belongs to the Strategy 1 rule, not this one: the a0 family constraint must hold

name: ping-allowlisted
why: ping opens the same raw ICMP socket; the comm allowlist alone must suppress it

name: unprivileged-icmp-datagram
why: modern ping uses SOCK_DGRAM ICMP sockets (net.ipv4.ping_group_range), which cannot sniff; it must not fire even from a non-allowlisted name

name: noop-execve
why: an ordinary ioctl(fd, TCGETS) by a routine process: an audited syscall (atomic.rules records ioctl) that shares neither the anchored syscall nor its arguments -- a sanity floor that must stay quiet
source: synthetic: a routine ioctl(TCGETS), an audited high-volume syscall used as a non-firing floor
